samples.summary: Acceptance criterion "`wafflebase login` still completes end to end against a backend that ignores both new parameters" is not met: the CLI refuses every callback whose `state` does not match its nonce, including the `state`-less callback an older backend sends. Against such a server login can only end in the 30-second timeout with the `sawUnboundCode` message (login.ts:242, 298-303) — it never completes. The task doc's own plan bullet (docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:41-45) is internally contradictory on this point ("a new CLI works against an old server" vs "a code that arrives with no `state` … is still refused"), and the AC at line 68-69 is the one that loses. Either the AC/doc must be restated (new CLI requires a nonce-echoing backend) or the CLI needs an explicit opt-in fallback.

The design doc asserts behavior the implementation does not have: "Both are optional on the wire, so a new CLI still works against a server that predates them", immediately followed by "When a code arrives with no `state` at all (which is what an older backend looks like), the CLI refuses it". Those two sentences cannot both be true — refusing the only callback an old backend sends means the login fails (30s timeout). The canonical login-flow spec is left self-contradictory for the next reader, and rest-api.md §7 repeats the "both optional" framing without noting that the CLI side is hard-fail.

Two unrelated tasks are landed as one change: the #661 error-envelope refactor (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md, ~30 CLI files) and the OAuth loopback binding (docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md, backend auth + CLI login). The loopback task doc itself says the first attempt "shipped inside the #661 error-envelope branch and was reverted for landing half-done … This is that work done as its own change" (lines 17-22), so re-bundling them contradicts the stated remediation and makes an independent revert of either half impossible again.

§10 Error Matrix was not updated for the new envelope emitters this change introduces/converts: `login` failures (UNAUTHORIZED), `ctx switch` (UNAUTHORIZED / NOT_FOUND), `schema` unknown name (NOT_FOUND), `files upload` STDIN_UNSUPPORTED / FILE_NOT_FOUND / FILE_TOO_LARGE / FILE_READ_FAILED, and the generic HTTP_ERROR fallback used by `backendErrorEnvelope`. §9 now claims every emitter produces the documented envelope, but the table that enumerates codes still lists only the old set.

samples.summary: `failFromBackend` emits `code: 'UNAUTHORIZED'` with `process.exit(1)`, but docs/design/cli.md §10 documents "Backend 401/403 → exit 2, UNAUTHORIZED" (and 5xx/network → exit 2, SYSTEM). Converting login's prose failures to the envelope was the chance to align the exit code with the documented matrix; as written an agent branching on exit code sees 1 for an auth failure the spec says is 2.

Skill files still show the error envelope in its old, unattributed form (`{ "error": { "code": "CONFIRMATION_REQ", "message": … } }` here, and docs-read-content.md:86 for TYPE_MISMATCH). Skills are the agent-facing contract per cli.md §8; after this change every such error also carries `command`, so the samples agents are told to expect are now stale.

`secretEquals` is a third hand-rolled constant-time comparison in the tree — packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts:59 already has the identical length-check + `timingSafeEqual` idiom in the same package, and packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:195 adds a fourth. At least the two backend copies could share one helper.

The risk table now documents `StateEntry.csrf` as a value "that nothing reads yet" rather than removing it. The loopback task explicitly puts this out of scope, so this is only a note: shipping a design doc that records dead state as a permanent caveat invites it to stay dead.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: login.ts:240-246 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, including `state === null` (the old-backend shape), without settling the callback promise; the only terminal path is the 30s timeout rejection at login.ts:293-308. auth.controller.ts:127-134 confirms a backend that ignores `nonce=` emits no `state`, so such a flow can never complete. The task doc checks off the acceptance criterion "`wafflebase login` still completes end to end against a backend that ignores both new parameters" (lines 68-69) while its own plan bullet (lines 41-45) states the no-`state` callback "is still refused" — an internal contradiction, and the AC is unmet. No opt-in fallback or bypass exists in the CLI. This is a spec-conformance failure against a named acceptance criterion, squarely in the design-fit lane and major (not a line-level logic bug).

verdict.reason: The quoted text exists verbatim at docs/design/cli.md:218-221 and is genuinely self-contradictory against the shipped code. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:240-246 rejects any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce — including `state === null` — with a 400 and keeps the listener open, so the only callback an older backend sends is never redeemed; login.ts:293-308 then fails after the 30s timer. There is no acceptance path for a stateless callback (test/login-callback.test.ts:25-28 asserts the 400), so "a new CLI still works against a server that predates them" is false, and the task's own acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:68-69, "login still completes end to end against a backend that ignores both new parameters") is unmet. docs/design/rest-api.md:338 repeats the "both are optional" framing without noting the CLI-side hard-fail. Canonical design-doc accuracy plus an unmet acceptance criterion is major under the design-fit rubric; no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.

finding.summary: docs/design/cli.md §9 now asserts "Every emitter builds it through `errorEnvelope` / `backendErrorEnvelope` … so 'one line, attributed' holds", but several CLI error paths still emit bare, unstructured text and bypass the envelope entirely: `login` (`console.error('Token exchange failed…')` L73, `'Failed to fetch user info.'` L90, `Failed to fetch workspaces…` L107, each followed by `process.exit(1)`) and `ctx switch` (`'Not logged in…'` L61, `Workspace not found: …` L67). The doc's universal claim is therefore not satisfied by the implementation — either narrow the claim to the enumerated paths or convert these emitters too.
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:73,90,107; packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:61,67 emit plain strings, not JSON envelopes.

verdict.reason: The finding's own cited locations show the opposite of what it claims. login.ts routes all three backend-failure paths through the envelope: it imports backendErrorEnvelope (L12) and calls failFromBackend at L83-87 ('Token exchange failed...'), L100-103 ('Failed to fetch user info.'), and L119-122 ('Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP ...)'); failFromBackend (L173-181) emits console.error(backendErrorEnvelope(body, fallback, command)) then process.exit(1). The quoted strings are `fallback` arguments to the envelope builder, not print arguments -- the reviewer appears to have matched message text and mistaken it for a bare console.error. The only plain console.error calls in login.ts are L57-58, the browser-open prompts, which the doc explicitly exempts as human prose. ctx.ts likewise imports errorEnvelope (L4) and both `ctx switch` failures use it with commandPath attribution: L63-69 (UNAUTHORIZED) and L75-77 (NOT_FOUND). Additionally the doc claim is not universal as represented: docs/design/cli.md:1051-1058 enumerates the non-throwing paths and names "the two session commands login and ctx switch" as being on the envelope path, while carving out prompts and success notices as prose. I swept every console.error( in packages/cli/src; the remainder are either envelope calls (formatter.ts:159, schema.ts:40, docs.ts:202,268,326, notes.ts:155,216, slides.ts:161,218) or console.error(line) progress-notice sinks (output/binary.ts:59, docs/content.ts:53, docs/import.ts:55, notes/content.ts:35, notes/import.ts:45, slides/content.ts:51, slides/import.ts:71, files/upload.ts:101) plus docs.ts:311 page-range warnings -- all display output the doc excludes. No bare, unstructured error emitter on the enumerated paths exists.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no task plan exists under docs/tasks/active/ for the OAuth nonce work. A conforming pair does exist: docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md and docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-lessons.md, matching the YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md / -lessons.md convention CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 requires. The todo is titled "CLI login: bind the loopback callback (nonce echo + PKCE)", references RFC 8252 §8.9 and RFC 7636, and its Plan enumerates the exact nonce work: CLI mints a 32-byte nonce and refuses non-matching state via constant-time compare (lines 26-29), PKCE challenge/verifier (30-31), GitHubAuthGuard ingestion with length bounds (32-35), AuthController echoing the nonce as state (36-37), plus Out-of-scope (53-61) and Acceptance criteria (63-69) sections and a docs line naming cli.md §3.1 and rest-api.md §7 (51). The todo also explains at lines 17-22 that a first attempt shipped inside the #661 error-envelope branch and was reverted to land as its own change, which accounts for the #661 envelope plan not mentioning login. A grep for "nonce" under docs/tasks/active returns exactly this pair, so the reviewer's stated searches should have surfaced it.
